newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening flat to firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening flat to firmer.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open flat to firmer on Monday, spurred by gains in platinum and palladium overnight on renewed concerns about Russian supplies, traders said.
COMEX June was gold was seen opening up $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce from Friday's close at $343.40 an ounce. Bullion was quoted at $341.95/$342.45.
In London gold was fixed at $342.15 Monday morning compared with $342.10 on Friday afternoon.
COMEX May silver was called to open flat to up 2.00 cents an ounce, compared to Friday's close at $4.713 an ounce.
The yellow metal market was also puzzled by reports that Russian central bank officials were visiting Tokyo to discuss with Japanese trading houses using gold to back Russian government bond issues.
Creating gold-backed bonds would suggest that Russia is looking to mobilize but not sell off its gold, analysts in London said overnight.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks slipped 616 ounces to 1,031,304 ounces Friday.
COMEX silver stocks fell 16,205 ounces to 189,872,972 ounces Friday.
NYMEX July platinum and NYMEX June palladium were called to open $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce firmer.
